x: Don MacLean had been given the first leg to Wandsworth Common and the first stroke of ten o'clock sent him on his way with nineteen other runners.
Don MacLean, now running more like his old self, finished second in the two mile event to Hugh Foord with a time of 9m.33.8s: other places:- K.
Don MacLean was our fastest man in the 2 miles, finishing 3rd in 9m.56s..Our other runners were K. Miller (10m4s.) David Jones(10m.22s.) and Ted Pallent(10m.50s.)

In the mile Derek Crookes gave a most welcome show of form by finishing third in a time of 4m.25·1s. Don Maclean also running well again did 4m.21s. and Alan Black 4m.25·7s. The standard in the long-jump was also high.
Don Maclean ran well in the first half of the race but when it became obvious that he wouldn't score he eased down to save himself for the steeplechase, in which he had volunteered to run.

Belgrave's only representative in the three miles was Don Maclean who recorded 14m.57·8s., and as the crowd left was seen to be reclining against a post in the centre of the arena in a rather deflated state - a fitting end to the day.
Yet another 4th place was recorded in the 3 miles where Pat Newell ran a creditable 14:23.8. Don Maclean was 12th in 15:23.

But Rangit was not to be beaten and they crossed the line to-gether, with a time of 14:52.5, a personal best for each. Don Maclean and Charlie Walker finished 6th & 7th, for the team to take the team award.
Following his now customary warm-up from dressing room to starting line Don Maclean duly took third place in the mile (after having borrowed some spikes) with a creditable 4:26.6.
Don Maclean was our only scorer in the three miles, finishing fifth after gaining two places in the last lap; thus gaining two valuable points.
During the second mile Pat broke away and was never again headed, while Don Maclean made one of his typical surges through the field to join the battle for 2nd. place with the other three.

Don Maclean who is in great form these days, went off last and with a good effort gained one place to bring us into fifth place. With a fit team we could have done better but in the circumstances the team ran well.

Clive Shippen, now almost fit again, held fifth place without losing ground on Woodford and handed over to Don Maclean for the final leg fifty seconds down on T.V.H. and thirty-three down on Woodford Green A.C.

Don Maclean soon went to the front and looked set for a record breaking run with Charlie Walker, Clive Shippen, Eric Gebbett, John Moore and Jumbo Masters forming one group, twenty yards up on Ranjit Bhatia, Len Bishop and Mike Stearman.

Don Maclean (17.55) Don was given this stage as a result of his fine last-leg efforts in the Poly and Surrey Road Relays. Although the task on this occasion was far more difficult as Woodford and Walton were 95 and 82 secs ahead, respectivly; the latter setting fastest time of the day.
With one and a half laps of this six lap race to go Don Maclean had snatched third place after running the first half of his leg at a blistering pace.
At one and a half miles Charlie Dabbs was 26th with Don Maclean close behind 34th, then came a gap before Alan Black 60th, Clive Shippen 62nd and Mal Robinson 68th, appeared.

These four were well backed up by Eric Gebbett, 22nd, Clive Shippen, 30th Mal Robinson, 31st and Don Maclean in 40th position. A mile later the positions were much the same with improvements by Clive and Mal, but a loss of seven places by Don.

Leaving the road and on to the golf-course the leading bunch of Dabbs, Newell, Moore and Robinson was led by Don Maclean. The furious pace set by Mac through the woods was too fast for John Moore, who dropped back to join Eric Gebbett and Clive Shippen fifty yards behind.

Don Maclean was having one of his days and was lying 120th and Alan Bishop completed our contingent in 125th place. The second half of the race produced an improvement in positions by the scoring six to the extent of approximately fifty places, but it was not enough to bring us anywhere near the pla…

At the halfway mark we still required two more runners to complete the team, but Don Maclean appeared in the nick of time to run 5th stage. Mike Stearman who had come only as a supporter, was press-ganged into running the last leg after 5 months of inactivity!
Don Maclean ran well, despite the agonised look on his face and the jack-tar sway of his body near the finish, but Terry Stacey had taken the Valley back into fourth place.
Generally speaking the race had run to the form book, although it is difficult to reconcile Don Maclean's 35:14 in 30th place with some of his better performances.
John Thresher and Don Maclean continued their winning way. At Wimbledon Park on June 14th, Belgrave (67 points) were beaten in the senior match by Surrey A.C.
For two laps the holder, Malcolm Robinson, led the field through the elements until Don Maclean took over with Pat Newell and John Davies on his heels.

Don Maclean and Clive Shippen reached the final (Clive 15:00 exactly!), but Arthur Bruce 15:06) just failed to make it. Unfortunately, both our qualifiers produced slower times in the final and were way down the field.
Don Maclean took on the last leg run and easily held our fifth place. He has never been known to bound over the summit of a hill this size in such fine fettle!
It was good to see Eric Gebbett out again after moving house, and also Don MaClean who seemed to have recovered well from the argument his "jalopy" had with a certain lamp-post!
Others like David Jones, Don Maclean, Ken Venton and our newly promoted Youths will be endeavouring to reach that "top 12" also, so a few fireworks would not be amiss!

Don Maclean in inimitable fashion appeared immediately after the start - it is a pity he cannot find a jalopy which could do the distance in a little faster time, we could then depend upon him reaching the starting line with at least a minute or two to spare!
Joe Dooley and Don MacLean completed our runners. Mac, not for the first time, tried to give the whole field a four minutes start and did well to finish where he did.

But for the ever-readiness of Joe Dooley and Don MacLean to fill gaps whenever called upon we would have been unable to finish a team. Injuries to Kerr, Dabbs and Davies and the absence of our usual spear-head,Pat Newell, did not augur well for our chances before we had even left London.
Don Maclean was in one of his "on form" moods for the last leg and ran well to gain one place - given another quarter of a mile he would have undoubtedly caught the Walton man ahead.

Unfortunately the course was a little on the hilly side for Don Maclean who waltzed rather than quick-stepped, and we had finally to be content with eighth place some fourteen seconds behind Mitcham's 7th.

STAGE XII - Don Maclean (17:50, 9th fastest) Don looking like a champion devoured the stretch across Preston Park and although naturally tiring at the end held on well to put up one of his best road performances for the Club and to give a pleasant surprise to all the doubting Thomases.
Others worthy of mention were Smithers (220 - 23.9, L.J. 19'9") Cornelius (220- 24.0 100 - 10.7), Don Maclean, Laurie O'Hara and Dave Baines.

Don Maclean had an unexpected 'good un' with Laurie O'Hara holding off clive Shippen for third place. In the Senior Field Events, we had our usual shortage of competitors, but this must in no way detract from the performances of young Derek Wade in the Long Jump.

John Davies beat Don Maclean in a tussle for second place with O'Hara closing on them at the finish. The most encouraging feature of this event was the number of 'lesser lights' who got inside sixteen minutes and showed that we have certain strength in depth.
Don Maclean was 3rd and Bill Kerr 7th. BOTTOM RIGHT: Alan Black who set a new Club Steeplechase record of 9:20.0 in the Scottish Championships.
Don Maclean who has been running far more consistently of late, pulled out all the stops in an effort to pull back the two Clubs ahead, but to no avail and we had to be content with 3rd position.
Even so, Portsmouth were still out of reach and Don Maclean only had to go through the formality of maintaining our comfortable second spot.

Don Maclean has this year been entrusted with last leg in all the relays in which we have competed and has aquitted himself admirably. This was to be no exception for although he could not catch T.V.H. he certainly gave Walton no chance of 3rd place.
BOTTOM CENTRE: Laurie O'Hara races for the final change-over. BOTTOM RIGHT: Don Maclean crosses the line just 65 secs. behind T.V.H.

Gerry celebrated his initiation by slicing a full ½ minute off the existing course record with 14:15. Other notable runs were made by Fairclough, O'Hara and Don Maclean; the latter's 15:11 being 2nd fastest of the day.

"Charlie boy" didn't look very happy leading Stage 4 with the result that Don Maclean took over with opponents hard on his heels. Don gave way to two of them and sent Gerry off to his whirlwind finish.

Don Maclean excelled himself to be our fourth scorer only a short distance behind John. Then came a gap before Ken Miller appeared--Ken is slowly working his way back afer a long lay off through injury and by the time the big races come round should be a great force again.

Laurie O'Hara was 5th, Pat Bradley 6th and Don Maclean 7th. Belgrave scored 16 pts to win easily from Poly, 28pts.and a team consisting of two Walton runners and a couple of Bank runners who scored 44 pts.

Close behind was Don Maclean (118) who made ground impressively in the latter stages to complete our scoring six. To finish 8th without Kerr, Linstead, Sawyer, Newell, Thresher and Roffey just shows what potentiality we really have, We can only hope our bad luck came all at once and that we shall ha…

No, this is not Don Maclean the cross-country runner being helped from the finishing line of the Orion 15 race, but Don Maclean the would-be rescuer after his brave effort to save a girl from the icy waters of the Thames on a cold February day.
Don Maclean, who was in the 270s, was soon made aware that he was now 6th scorer and he immediately set about the opposition in "Linstead fashion".

Cooke could only increase his lead over Don Maclean by 6 seconds and it was here that Mitcham burst into the limelight once more through a fine run by Harvey (18:13) who took his team into 2nd place 7 seconds ahead of the Bels.

Don Maclean was now 6th, the long descent of Copse Hill being tailor-made for his raking stride. Dave Cocks and Chris Steer were still in the hunt but beginning to show signs of strain whilst Charlie Dabbs was still looking strong and obviously waiting for the hilly return journey.

This was the position that faced Don Maclean for the last leg - a situation of complete isolation. No hope of catching any of the teams ahead and equally safe from Birchfield who were holding 6th place.
Don Maclean is another to have been pinned down at long last.

We fielded four teams and would surely have won the team race if one more of our better runners had been able to turn out. As it was,Don Maclean was called upon to back up Bill Kerr and Laurie O'Hara. We were only beaten by one point for third team place.
Charlie Smart (still going very strongly at the age of 55!), Gordon Biscoe, Don Maclean (one of his off days), George Piddington and Chris Keavey completed our two teams.
Jack Brown also ran well and will no doubt be picking up many Vets prizes come his 40th birthday in August. John Dear,Don Maclean and the "Dukes Joggers" completed our two teams. 153 finished.
Our other runners-up were Don Maclean in the mile (4:29.5) and Tony Fairclough in the 3 miles (14:44.4). It's good to see Tony getting down to work again.
Everything depended on Don Maclean over the last stage and no-one envied him his task--Maynard of Cambridge H. 46seconds ahead and Malcolm Browne, the Essex Beagle miler, just 20seconds behind.

Only 4 of our expected six appeared and Jack Brown and Don Maclean were moved up to fill the gap. Both ran very well, but we were obliged to concede 53 seconds to Blackheath at the end and had to be content with 3rd place.

Don Maclean really excelled himself in winning the 2 miles and recording 9:19.0 which must be his best for a good many years. There must be something in this marriage lark,for all this season Mac has been cutting down his times on the track.

Don Maclean who completed the team had one of his off days and was mot amused on entering the straight to hear himself announced as - "Another runner wearing those well known colours of that famous club - Coventry Godiva".
Don Maclean arriving soon after the main party thus found himself some two hours early for the start of a race instead of his customary 2 mins or less!
Eric Penny and Chris Keavey again continued to show an improvement, whilst Don Maclean found the course, the heat and achilles trouble a little too much for one afternoon.
Our subject is,of course, the winner of that race - Donald G.Maclean - and it is worth noting that his team mate on this occasion was Ian H.Boyd, a subsequent international and Olympian.

Don Maclean started about 12 minutes behind the feild but was unable to catch any tail-enders in the next 42 minutes. At least he must have enjoyed it more than Bob Glover and Peter Wrench who went off course and were not recorded in!

Everyone had a good time, particularly Bob Taylor who celebrated his birthday with Don Maclean in the bar! Chris put a lot of time into preparation for the evening and deserves commendation for his decor, publicity and presentation---not forgetting, of course, Charlie Manning's witty skits on T.V. a…

The most inspiring event of the afternoon was the 3000m Steeplechase, won by John Dear, but with the amazing Don Maclean only 16 seconds down in 2nd place and beating all the other clubs' 'A' runners., a tremendous feat by our hard working Press Secretary.
Don Maclean may have been last to arrive at the track but the momentum of his speedy change and dash to the start carried him into a first lap lead, closely tailed by the barefooted Trevor Hart.
Don Maclean showed he is returning to fitness by beating drinking partner Chris Keavey and Gordon Biscoe, who was still looking rather flushed after his exertions during the afternoon.
Ranjit finds thirst to be more of a problem than fatigue. Funny---so do Don Maclean and Linstead!
Replying on behalf of the Club Don Maclean said Belgrave had had it's ups and downs, and since the war it had been mainly downs, until recently.
In the Belgrave Handicap,"old-stagers" Don Maclean and Mike Stearman tied for first place Third was that scourge of the handicapper, Jim Rimmer - he'll have his wings removed altogether soon!
In the 'B' team Don Maclean set out to prove that he should have been nominated for the 'A' team and this he did very easily by finishing in front of two 'A' team nominees.

Not to be outdone in this sort of practice,Don Maclean set off no less than 12:15 in arrears! A first circuit of 19:00 indicated that he was not going out for a win and he politely informed the officials that they needn't wait up for him!

Shippen: There will of course be a rebate for Old Age Pensioners and those who are chronically sick. Mr. Donald Maclean (Oxford and Cambridge): If you think I'm actually going to pay money for that libellous rag ...

Ron Linstead's camera portrays the agony of the effort (Clive Shippen) and the pleasure of the reward (Don Maclean). There is no truth in the story that Don renews his strength by drinking Courage -- he drinks it simply because £100 was tucked in his shoes!
A new name was added to those who have held the 'Denmark Pot' when on December 2nd, the Belgrave Dart Championship went to Don Maclean, who gained a narrow victory over Dave McMillan.

PETER and MARGARET HILLIAR and DON and JENNY MacLEAN are hearing the patter of tiny feet ... again. Spectating at the Club Championships was none other than our 800 metre record holder DAVE COCKS with two year old daughter ELIZABETH.

Don MacLean always used to be most adamant that we should never have women members but recently he was heard to say: "My children can do what they like - they don't have to do athletics, they don't have to train but if they are going to join a club it's GOT to be Belgrave.

Well done Don Maclean, who has managed to get his name on the "Denmark Pot" by winning our Darts Championship. It is particularly appropriate that Don should win this event at last for he was one of its instigators some dozen or so years ago.

I think there were no two opinions when Don Maclean, Bob Taylor and I agreed that Belgrave Harriers embody what might be regarded as the best aspects of Athletics from every point of view and one hopes very much that the Club would continue to thrive as it has done in the past hundred years.
Don Maclean · Mar 63
We regret to record the death of Don Maclean who died recently following an accident.
We wonder if dear old Don Maclean, sadly no longer with us, ever dreamed in 1963 that the Pot he presented would be held in such high regard for so long.

Our Juniors were a solid 5th with Charlie Walker 24th while our Youths were runners up with Don Maclean a good 4th in the individual. The National Cross Country Champs in March only reflected for Belgrave their previous performances.

We were clear winners from Herne Hill and our juniors, led by Don Maclean finished 6th. The Club Ten Mile Championship following the Counties was won by Jack Brown from Charlie Walker and Bill Lucas, confirming our hopes for the big races ahead.
The Seniors, led home by Les Stokell were 8th; the Juniors with Charlie Walker in 40th place were 21st and the Youths with Don Maclean in 18th place were 7th.

Bill and Don MacLean inaugurated the Denmark Pot Darts championship as far back as 1963 and Bill has had an enviable eleven wins. One extremely amusing incident occurred when Bill was on holiday on the Norfolk Broads.
Don Maclean presented the “Pot” as the trophy for our Darts Championship in 1963 with the first competition taking place in the Club Room in The King of Denmark.
